articles.title: Truemetrics (YC S23) Is Hiring in Berlin – GTM Lead
articles.originalTitle: Truemetrics (YC S23) Is Hiring in Berlin – GTM Lead
articles.excerpt:
Join truemetrics - Build technology to navigate the world

truemetrics helps organizations to navigate the world more efficiently. We are solving one of the biggest pain points in last mile delivery: how to get parcels, groceries, and food to the right door faster and more efficiently.

Our technology sits in the smartphone of the courier and understands where they park, walk and enter a building. Our technology is right now mapping locations in Germany, Qatar, the UK, Denmark, Sweden, Poland, the Netherlands and many other countries.

Our traction

YC-backed, profitable, and past €1.5M ARR - selling to enterprise carriers like GLS, DPD, and PostNord. The core works. Now the job is the take-off from €1M to €10M+: strengthening what's working today (the now) and discovering what's next (the new).

Who we are

We are a tech-driven, customer-obsessed company with a small but highly skilled team, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in mapping and positioning.

You'll work directly with the two founders. Ingo (CEO), a serial founder with a background in engineering and tech consulting, leads go-to-market and customers. Jan (CTO), with a PhD in control theory and a decade of engineering experience, leads tech and product.

We thrive on autonomy, ownership, and speed—which means we're looking for curious problem-solvers who love tackling hard challenges and making an immediate impact. If you want structure, rigid processes, and a slow corporate environment, this is not the place for you.



The role

You work directly with the founders - no layer in between - and you your focus will be to answer the question: what should truemetrics sell next, and how do we sell it. You'll form a point of view, prove it with real customers, and be accountable for turning the answer into something repeatable. That plays out along two paths:

Path 1 — Discover the next wedge (the new). Product and market innovation in and around logistics: new products from the data we already own, new use cases for our tech beyond parcel delivery, and where delivery is heading next. You research a space, form a point of view, test it with customers, and help build what works.

Path 2 — Run and strengthen the core business (the now). Support ongoing customer projects, onboard new customers, and push truemetrics into new geographies. Get on-site with COOs, ride along with drivers, and crack our hardest question: why better data doesn't always translate into operational impact - and what unlocks the take-off.

You won't be handed a playbook - you'll write one.

Your first 90 days

  - By day 30 — immerse. Learn the product cold, ride along with drivers, sit in on customer POCs and sales calls, and map our pipeline and deals. Understand firsthand why better data doesn't always translate into take-off - and start forming your own hypotheses.
  - By day 60 — get your hands dirty. Take real ownership of a live customer project or a wedge worth investigating, and start pressure-testing where the next chunk of revenue could come from - directly with customers.
  - By day 90 — bring a bet. Present a validated point of view on what we should sell next and how, with a plan - and be running at least one real thread end to end (a deal, a new geography, or a validated new wedge).

What we're really looking for

Two things matter more than any specific background:

  - You originate. You don't just analyze options or wait for direction - you form a point of view, commit to a bet, and drive it. When you see a problem, your instinct is "here's what I'd do," not "here are five things one could consider."
  - You have real commercial drive. You're energized by the selling and building side - talking to customers, running deals, opening new markets - not just studying them from a distance. You want to be in the arena.

Beyond that:

  - Fast, flexible, and sharp. You context-switch well, get up to speed on a new company or problem quickly, and are comfortable with ambiguity and a half-defined scope.
  - Comfortable in the real world. You can sit with a COO in the morning and ride along with a driver in the afternoon, and speak both languages. You're drawn to operational reality, not just slides.
  - Strong communicator and self-starter. High autonomy, low hand-holding.
  - Based in Berlin with a valid work permit. This is a full-time, on-site role (home-office 1 days/week is normal) working closely with the founders.

Who thrives here

We're open on background - the two must-haves above matter more than any résumé line. But this role is built for A-players who've done something like this before. People who tend to thrive here are:

  - Ex-founders who've built and sold, and want to go zero-to-one again without carrying the whole company alone.
  - GTM or commercial leaders who have personally driven a step-change - taken a product from early traction to real scale, cracked a hard market, or built a motion from scratch.
  - Top-tier operators who've led a transformation and want a bigger canvas: prior Founders Associate / EiR, ex-consultants who actually owned outcomes, or logistics/operations leaders ready to build rather than run.

If you've done the hard version of this before and want to do it again with more ownership and more upside, we want to hear from you.



Why join us?

  - Real impact. Your work ships into production and moves the company's direction - visibly, fast.
  - Direct founder access. Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the founding team, no bureaucracy.
  - Ownership from day one. The right person won't take a predefined template - you'll push back and have your own idea of what this should be. We expect that, and we give you a say.
  - Backed by the best. Y Combinator, Soma Capital, Rebel Fund, and other top investors.
  - Pick your own hardware. Yearly budget - buy what you want and keep it.
  - Equity package. You're playing a key role; you should share in the upside. A meaningful equity package is planned for this position alongside salary.

Why NOT to join us?

If you need a team to help you got things done, a slow pace, if you are uncomfortable with uncertainty, or a job where you can coast without ownership, this isn't it. We move fast, iterate quickly, and expect everyone to contribute with initiative and creativity.

How to apply

  - Include your CV.
  - Tell us why you're a great fit - be specific. Bonus: point to a time you originated something and drove it yourself, not as part of a defined playbook.

articles.title: Roame (YC S23) Is Hiring Lead Engineer
articles.originalTitle: Roame (YC S23) Is Hiring Lead Engineer
articles.excerpt:
About Roame

Roame is a flight and hotel search engine for points and miles.

Booking business or first class with points instead of cash saves travelers thousands of dollars on a single trip. The hard part is finding the seats. Award space is scattered across dozens of airline and hotel programs, it moves constantly, and the best deals get taken. Doing it by hand means hours across a dozen browser tabs, and often days.

Roame finds those deals in seconds. Members also book hotels through us and get our commission rebated back to them immediately. Roame was founded by Tim and Zi. Tim spent the previous decade covering consumer and travel companies on the hedge fund side. Zi ran data encryption systems at Airbnb.

We started Roame after losing dozens of hours hunting for first class award space to Asia across a dozen browser tabs. Award travel is a data problem. Humans shouldn't have to solve it by hand.

Why join Roame now?

  - Profitable. We run on revenue, not runway. We can start multi year technical work and actually finish it.
  - Loved product. We're the default tool for a lot of the points and miles community, and our users are vocal about it.
  - Scope. This is the top engineering role at the company. There is no larger org above it.
  - AI native. A large share of our engineering is agent assisted and our whole workflow is built around it.

About the role

  - Own engineering at Roame. You would be the most senior engineer here, reporting to the founders.
  - Set technical direction across our Go backend and web app. We also ship a native iOS app, and every API decision has an iOS client on the other end of it. You need to account for that, not build it.
  - Finish our move to a modern Go service architecture and retire what's left of the old one.
  - Own correctness where money moves: booking, checkout, payments.
  - Set the engineering bar on testing, review, documentation, and hiring.
  - Grow into the senior most technical role at the company as we scale.

How we work

  - Write it down before building it. Specs and architecture live in the repo.
  - Test first. Most work starts from a written test plan.
  - Ship in small increments. Days, not sprints.
  - Nothing waits until tomorrow if it can go out today.
  - Disagree out loud, early, to the person. Then pick something and move.
  - No task is beneath anyone.
  - Spoon feed yourself, learning is free, generate a video from the code and learn it

Your first 90 days

  - Week 1. Ship something to production. Small is fine. Nobody here spends a week reading code before they touch it.
  - Day 30. You own a meaningful piece of the booking and checkout path and have shipped a significant update to it.
  - Day 60. You own the migration plan. Your sequencing, your call on what gets cut.
  - Day 90. A major piece of our legacy architecture is retired, and you know exactly what it takes to finish off the rest.

On AI

We use it constantly and we want someone who loves it as much as we do.

AI writes great code and it writes bad code, sometimes in the same file. Getting the good version every time is the actual skill, and it's the one we're hiring for. Knowing what to specify up front. Knowing when a human has to stay in the loop. Knowing when to throw the output away instead of patching it. Building the guardrails that make good output the default instead of the lucky case.

Our habits around specs and tests exist because they're what make agent assisted work trustworthy at speed.

What we're looking for

  - 4 to 6+ years of engineering experience, post-grad
  - Confident you're a 10x engineer, and able to tell us why.
  - Strong in Go and comfortable in TypeScript. Mobile experience isn't required, but you should think in terms of a mobile client when you design an API.
  - You've owned a system and answered for it when it broke, you understand resilience
  - You've finished a hard migration, not just started one.
  - You've shipped code that moved real money.
  - Opinions about how engineering teams should run that stuck somewhere before.
  - You want to lead without giving up writing code.
  - You understand distributed engineering
  - You understand that this is a living, breathing system; hours keep it moving; this isn’t a 40 hours a week job

Probably not a fit

  - You want every day to be greenfield. This is a three year old codebase with real debt.
  - You'd rewrite before you understand.
  - You need priorities handed to you.
  - You cannot distinguish between slop and non-slop.
  - You're comfortable letting something sit until next sprint.
  - You bite off more than you can chew; unable to strategically land impact and releases.
  - You have a general disinterest for travel
  - You’re easily frustrated by hard problems

Technology

Go, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Postgres, Protobuf. Swift on iOS, which you won't be expected to write.

$175-250k base depending on experience and location in the US

0.5%-2% equity

articles.title: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction
articles.originalTitle: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction
articles.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) have become the default tool for a remarkable range of tasks, yet they have had conspicuously little success at one of the most common machine learning workloads: predictive analytics over tabular data. This gap is the founding premise of the fast-growing field of tabular foundation models, but the question of why generic LLMs fail has remained open. We study a frontier LLM in its purest inference regime - a single generation pass over a prompt containing the full training and test data, with no tools, no agentic scaffolding, and no fine-tuning - and systematically evaluate five hypotheses for the failure: (a) an inability to handle noisy or non-linearly-separable data; (b) the linearised CSV format obscuring column structure; (c) the tokenisation of numeric values; (d) the number of test points classified per query; and (e) the dimensionality of the input. Controlled experiments falsify (a)-(d). Dimensionality, in contrast, is decisive: sweeping random linear projections of thirty-one benchmark datasets, the LLM is the only method among nine whose accuracy decreases as dimensionality grows, while every classical baseline stays flat or improves. A behavioural comparison against 252 configured classical models finds that in two dimensions the LLM predicts like a local, distance-based method (up to 91.6% grid agreement), but in higher dimensions no classical model - even when augmented with tuned, dimension-dependent noise - reproduces its predictions. We do not claim to have identified the internal mechanism; our results show, more modestly, that the LLM's capability dissolves with dimension in a way no noise-corrupted classical learner mimics - which explains why LLMs, so capable elsewhere, keep losing to fifty-year-old baselines on tables, while leaving the mechanism of the prediction as an open question.

articles.title: Galaktyka Andromedy coraz wolniej tworzy gwiazdy
articles.originalTitle: Galaktyka Andromedy coraz wolniej tworzy gwiazdy
articles.excerpt: Zespół astronomów pracujący pod kierunkiem Tobina M. Wainera z Uniwersytetu Waszyngtońskiego opublikował w The Astrophysical Journal najdokładniejszą jak dotąd mapę niedawnej historii formowania się gwiazd w Galaktyce Andromedy (M31) – naszym najbliższym wielkim sąsiedzie w Grupie Lokalnej. Praca opiera się na danych z przeglądu PHAST (Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Southern Treasury), podczas którego po raz pierwszy południową część dysku M31 zbadano równie precyzyjnie, co część północną, przeanalizowaną wcześniej w ramach przeglądu PHAT (Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Treasury).

articles.title: CollectWise (YC F24) Is Hiring
articles.originalTitle: CollectWise (YC F24) Is Hiring
articles.excerpt:
About Us

CollectWise is a fast growing and well funded Y Combinator-backed startup. We’re using generative AI to automate debt collection, a $35B market in the US alone. Our AI agents are already outperforming human collectors by 2X, and we’re doing so at a fraction of the cost.

With a team of five, we scaled to a $2 million annualized run rate in just a few months, and we are now hiring an AI Agent Engineer to help us reach $10 million within the next year.

About the role

CollectWise is hiring an AI Agent Engineer to build the infrastructure, prompting systems, and core architecture behind our voice AI agents. You will work at the intersection of AI infrastructure, prompt engineering, conversational design, and product development to build voice agents that power millions of consumer interactions.

This is a highly technical role for someone who is equally comfortable building production-grade systems, writing and refining prompts and conversation flows, and designing rigorous testing frameworks to maximize real-world performance. You should be analytical, business-minded, and motivated by measurable outcomes.

What you’ll do

  - Build our voice AI infrastructure in LiveKit
  - Design and own the architecture of our real-time voice agent systems, including orchestration, state management, latency optimization, prompting and reliability.
  - Own the end-to-end prompting strategy for CollectWise voice agents, including conversation flows, tone, compliance-safe phrasing, guardrails, and edge-case handling.
  - Build and maintain testing and evaluation frameworks for voice agent performance, including A/B testing, regression testing, conversation QA, benchmarking, and KPI reporting.
  - Write, expand, and improve our core AI prompting to cover more real-world scenarios.
  - Continuously iterate based on performance data, call outcomes, and customer feedback to improve containment, conversion, liquidation rates, and customer satisfaction.
  - Optimize ASR, STT, TTS, turn-taking, interruption handling, and state transitions to improve voice quality and agent performance.
  - Build scalable systems and tooling to support millions of voice interactions.
  - Migrate client implementations from legacy voice AI infrastructure to the latest systems you build, while preserving client-specific customizations and workflows.
  - Develop prompt and agent tooling, including versioning, rollout strategies, monitoring, safety checks, and debugging workflows.
  - Work closely with product, operations, and leadership to translate business goals into high-performing voice agent behavior.

What we’re looking for

  - 2+ years of experience in voice AI, conversational AI, prompt engineering, speech systems, or related agentic workflows.
  - 3+ years of experience in platform, infrastructure, or backend engineering.
  - Strong experience with Node.js, AWS, and SQL.
  - Experience building and shipping production systems in a startup or similarly fast-paced environment.
  - Experience with voice orchestration platforms or agent frameworks such as LiveKit.
  - Strong prompt writing instincts and the ability to design clear, effective, and resilient conversational flows.
  - Strong analytical skills and comfort tying technical work directly to business outcomes and ROI.
  - Excellent communication skills, high ownership, and a strong work ethic.

Nice to have

  - Experience with SIP trunking, telephony infrastructure, and production voice systems.
  - Experience working with real-time audio pipelines, call routing, and carrier or telephony integrations.
  - Familiarity with speech infrastructure in production environments.

Compensation

  - Salary: $200,000 to $300,000, depending on experience and qualifications
  - Equity: 0.25% to 1%
